ImageDescription.value: Wiyot elders, tribal members and people holding candles around a firepit at the last Wiyot Vigil in memory of the massacre-interrupted World Renewal Ceremony in 1860 on Tuluwat, also called "Indian Island" and "Gunther Island."  The Wiyots were nearly annihiliated but eventually regained federal recognition in the late 1950s and a portion of the island in the 2000s; in part by purchase and in part by an unprecedented return of land to the tribe from the city of Eureka.  Finally after years of environmental cleanup, the tribe announced that this would be the last annual vigil because the World Renewal Ceremony would resume at the end of March 2014 for the first time in over 150 years.  The grove of trees to the right over the heads of participants is on Tuluwat itself, the vigils were held for over 20 years at Woodley Island Marina adjacent to the National Historic Register Monument marker. The only available light for this hand held image was the firepit.

Categories.value: Femicide|Violence against women|Sutton, London|White ribbons|White ribbons opposing violence against women|Say Her Name|Feminist art|Self-published work|March 2022 in London|Colorful benches|Art in the London Borough of Sutton|2022 in the London Borough of Sutton|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation (51° N, 1° W)|Mosaics in London|Murder of Sarah Everard|Memorial benches in the London Borough of Sutton

ImageDescription.value:
This memorial bench was installed on Trinity Square, Sutton High Street on Friday 4th March 2022 and unveiled in a dedication ceremony by the Mayor of Sutton Patricia Fivey.

The mosaic design is a based on two sketches by each artist which they combined to make one whole. Hearts and flowers surround a main heart with angel wings and a golden thread connects the parts. Glass tessarae were used throughout apart from the hand-made ceramic letter tiles that read:

"Never commit, excuse or remain silent" with a white ribbon tile to reflect the White Ribbon pledge. "Remembering women who died from male violence"

The mosaic was made in reverse and set with anthracite grey grout then sealed with two layers of Eco Epoxy UVPoxy resin to protect the mosaic beneath. It took approximately 200 hours to design and make.

The project was led by Sarah McGuinness, Chair of Reclaim Sutton's Streets and supported by Sutton Council and Successful Sutton BID

Samia Tossio and Sarah McGuinness had connected over a yarn bombed Tree of Remembrance and a candle-lit vigil for Sabina Nessa in 2021.

Conversations around making a permanent memorial followed and the mosaic memorial bench was the outcome. The unveiling coincided with the first anniversary of the murder of Sarah Everard and International Women's Day. Coverage of the dedication ceremony made ITV London news with articles in many national and regional newspapers including The Independent and The Guardian.

Artist.value: Samia Tossio

ImageDescription.value: A photo of two activists holding lighted candles (one visible in a woman's hand, the other hidden by the other hand of the man holding it) at a vigil held outside the Bahrain embassy in London on day 37 of democracy activist Ali Mushaima's hunger strike. A week earlier, Ali Mushaima had been taken to St. Thomas' Hospital over mounting fears for his health after his blood sugar fell to a dangerously low level. Three days earlier the well known activist Zeinab al-Khawaja also joined the hunger strike. Ali Mushaima's hunger strike was on behalf of his father, Hassan Mushaima, a political prisoner detained in Bahrain since 2011.

Credit.value: Vigil for Bahraini hunger strikers.

Artist.value: Alisdare Hickson from Canterbury, United Kingdom
